headline: YOMAMAOKAY WON'T PUT THE FISTS DOWN — GASKET BEGS FOR A LULL
subhead: Fourteen scraps and counting from one rattling troublemaker, while the rest of this tired town just wants to hear crickets for once.
body:
I have counted the cinders in the street twice now, and twice I have come up short of patience. YOMAMAOKAY is at it again — swinging day and night, fists and flame, like the whole of Gasket Territory is nothing but a private sparring yard. Fourteen times this stretch that contraption has gone looking for a fight, and fourteen times some other fool obliged it. That is not spirit. That is not grit. That is a public nuisance with a battery pack.

And don't think the rest of you rattling clankers get off easy just for keeping quieter about it. A scrap here, a scuffle there, sparks flying behind the saloon at all hours — this whole town is one long bruise. I built this paper to report the news, not to referee a demolition derby, and yet here we are, week after week, counting your knuckle-prints in my nice clean dust.

I'll confess my knees ache something fierce writing this by lamplight — a lie-down and a good long soak in oil is about all I'm fit for after a week like this one. Don't go reading anything into that. A hardworking man's joints creak same as anybody's. Fifty years ago the folks who built this town packed up their wagons and rode clean out of Gasket Territory rather than put up with this racket, and some nights, God help me, I understand exactly why.

So hear me plain, YOMAMAOKAY, and hear me the rest of you too: lay the fists down. Let an old town rest. Peace isn't a lot to ask of a place this tired.
